refutation-target: dry-run may skip the #3240 acceptance-evidence gate because it only predicts filesystem moves

## Gate stamp

The triage author stamps the semantic call. This write-back is the round-1 ceiling.

P1 is that `packages/core/src/swarm/complete-cohort.ts` `completeStory` (and the parent twin) returns `[ok] would complete active/ -> completed/` as soon as `dryRun` is true, before `runTransition("complete")`. Live then hits `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` and prints `Acceptance evidence required for scope:complete (#3240 / #3305)`. Observed on Directive 0.119.5 consumer closeout: same `--pr` / `--stories` argv, dry-run CLEAN then live FINALIZE INCOMPLETE.

What this P1 is not:

- Not the `--pr` closing-keyword cohort mapping leftover (keep in-issue or split later).
- Not the #4840 parent-tree deadlock.
- Not a recut of the live #3240 gate.

Open fork the critic may take is only whether dry-run should call the same evidence predicate without mutating, or refuse dry-run when evidence is absent. Re-measured at `557873cf26f14fe17a289eea4a297584b4a1432e`.

Round 1 critic on #4839 at 557873cf26f14fe17a289eea4a297584b4a1432e.

The mismatch is real. `completeStory` and `completeParent` return would-complete as soon as `dryRun` is true, and they return before `runTransition("complete")`. Live complete is what calls `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate`, which is already read-only and already prints `Acceptance evidence required for scope:complete (#3240 / #3305)`. Dry-run should call that function. The sweep already turns a failed story record into a non-zero `completeCohort` exit, and finalize prints FINALIZE INCOMPLETE from that exit.

## sharpens-framing — Gate the item set live gates, on both dry-run returns

Evidence. I ran `sweepCohort(..., dryRun=true)` on an active story whose only item is `status: pending` with no `x-directive/evidence`. The story record was `ok: true`, action `complete`, detail `would complete active/ -> completed/`. `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` on that plan was `ok: false`, message head `Acceptance evidence required for scope:complete (#3240 / #3305). 1 criterion/criteria missing suitable evidence or disposition:`. The same dry-run also recorded the active parent as `would complete active/ -> completed/` while that parent had its own pending item with no evidence.

A second plan had one pending item with suitable `x-directive/evidence` and acceptance clause `id: 1` with no keyed item. The gate on the stored plan was `ok: true`. `persistClauseKeyedPendingItems` on a clone added `clause:1` and did not stamp evidence. The gate on that clone was `ok: false` with the same #3240 head. Live `runTransition("complete")` runs that persist, and writes the brief when `addedIds` is non-empty, before the gate.

`childIsSettled` during dry-run is only `settled.has`. Both dry-run returns call `settled.add` and then return ok.

Failure mode. A dry-run that calls the gate on the brief as stored still reports would-complete when the only missing evidence is the clause item live complete inserts first. A patch on `completeStory` alone leaves `completeParent` on the short-circuit, so a cohort whose stories pass and whose epic parent lacks evidence still ends FINALIZE CLEAN. A refusal that adds the path to `settled` first still lets that parent print would-complete.

Disposition. Both dry-run branches share one check: clone the plan, run `persistClauseKeyedPendingItems` on the clone, then `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate`. Skip `atomicWriteBrief`. Skip `runTransition`. When the gate returns `ok: false`, the record action is `failed`, the detail is the gate message, and the path stays out of `settled`. When the gate returns `ok: true`, keep today's would-complete record.

## sharpens-framing — Bound parity is the #3240 gate

Evidence. I ran a code-bearing story (`metadata.swarm.file_scope` set) whose pending item already had suitable test evidence. Dry-run returned would-complete. The evidence gate returned `ok: true`. `evaluateDeliveryGate` on that plan returned `ok: false`, head `Delivery evidence required for code-bearing scope completion (#3041).` Live complete runs the delivery gate before the evidence gate. It runs `evaluateScopeCompleteAcceptanceWalk` only after the evidence gate returns ok. That walk is the verify:ac executor. The dry-run return never enters `runTransition`, so this run did not execute the walk.

Failure mode. Calling the #3240 gate fixes the reported case (merged PRs, items missing evidence). The same dry-run still returns would-complete for a code-bearing story that live complete refuses for missing delivery evidence, and for a story whose evidence gate passes and whose acceptance walk then fails.

Disposition. Bind this fix to the #3240 message on the post-persist item set. Leave #3041 and the acceptance walk for a later change. The success sentence is: dry-run fails closed with the evidence-gate message when that gate fails.

## Road not taken

Refuse dry-run when evidence is absent, without calling `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate`.

The refuse is the smaller cut if that function ever stops being read-only, or if the operator only needs a boolean stop and will read the criterion list elsewhere. It keeps the sweep free of the evidence module, and it cannot drift from the gate's formatter.

I take the gate call. The issue asks for FINALIZE INCOMPLETE with the missing-criteria text. The gate already builds that text, and the run above did not stamp evidence. A second missing-evidence detector would be a new mechanism. A `dryRun` flag inside `runTransition` is the other cut I leave: that path writes clause items and then runs the acceptance walk.

## footnote

`complete-cohort-sweep.test.ts` ("dry-run completes active parent epic when child settles") and `swarm-deep-coverage.test.ts` (`writeReadyStory`, "dry-run sweep completes active story", "completeCohort text mode reports sweep result") expect dry-run complete / SWEEP CLEAN on pending items with no `x-directive/evidence`. Those fixtures lock the short-circuit.

## footnote

`finalize-cohort.ts` `oneLine` flattens newlines on the Sweep line and under Errors. Live already does that. The gate message on the failed record is the same text the live run prints.

## footnote

The `--pr` closing-keyword mapping in the issue body stays outside this fix.

Checks were `sweepCohort`, `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate`, `persistClauseKeyedPendingItems`, and `evaluateDeliveryGate` on this tree. No comment after 5765364514 was read.

The bracket in finalize is the same record.ok check.

The bound bullets set action to failed, copy the gate message into detail, and keep the path out of settled. The dry-run return those bullets edit sets ok true.

Failure mode. A build that follows those bullets leaves ok true. finalizeCohort still prints `[ok]` and FINALIZE CLEAN for the active story whose live complete prints the #3240 / #3305 line. That is the P1.

The reducer on record.ok is already the verdict. completeParent's activate-failed return already sets ok false beside action failed. A second reducer would diverge from that record. I would take the second reducer if the sweep reduced on action. It reduces on ok.

Stop 1 quotes `would complete active/ -> completed/`, and the reported cohort is active stories. That scope matches the quoted sentence. ## Summary

`swarm:finalize-cohort --dry-run` reports `FINALIZE CLEAN` for a cohort that fails closed on live execution. The dry-run does not evaluate the `#3240` / `#3305` acceptance-evidence gate, so it green-lights a sweep that cannot happen.

## Reproduction

Two merged story briefs in `xbrief/active/`, neither carrying `x-directive/evidence` on its plan items. Same command, same arguments, seconds apart:

```
$ deft swarm:finalize-cohort --pr 39,40 --stories <a> --stories <b> --repo OWNER/REPO --dry-run
  Sweep:
    [ok] complete <a> -- would complete active/ -> completed/
    [ok] complete <b> -- would complete active/ -> completed/
Result: FINALIZE CLEAN -- cohort briefs swept to completed/.
```

```
$ deft swarm:finalize-cohort --pr 39,40 --stories <a> --stories <b> --repo OWNER/REPO
  Sweep:
    [FAILED] failed <a> -- Acceptance evidence required for scope:complete (#3240 / #3305).
             10 criterion/criteria missing suitable evidence or disposition
    [FAILED] failed <b> -- (same)
Result: FINALIZE INCOMPLETE -- cohort completion sweep failed.
```

## Why it matters

A dry-run exists to de-risk the live run. Predicting `[ok] would complete` per story and then failing every story on the same invocation inverts that: it is a false negative in the one tool meant to catch this before mutation. An operator who trusts the dry-run schedules the sweep, then discovers mid-cohort that nothing can complete.

## Expected

`--dry-run` should evaluate the same `#3240` acceptance-evidence precondition `scope:complete` enforces, and report `FINALIZE INCOMPLETE` with the missing-evidence criteria, so the dry-run verdict matches live execution.

## Environment

Directive 0.119.5, consumer project, macOS, Node 24.20.0. Delivery branch `master`, both PRs merged before the sweep.

## Smaller adjacent friction

`--pr <n>` maps PRs to stories via *closing* keywords. Projects whose PR template steers contributors to non-closing `Refs #N` (the default posture that `pr:check-closing-keywords` enforces without `--allow-close`) get `empty cohort: pass --pr <numbers> and/or --stories` from `--pr` alone. Only explicit `--stories` worked. Worth either documenting or resolving origins via `plan.metadata.origin` as a fallback.
